candidates.name: Naval Outlying Landing Field Joe Williams

source_notes.title: NAVFAC Site Descriptions - Naval Outlying Landing Field (NOLF) Joe Williams
source_notes.note: Official NAVFAC page says NOLF Joe Williams supports NAS Meridian, was formerly outlying field Bravo, was renamed in 1987, and is currently operated by NAS Meridian Air Operations.

source_notes.title: Final Community Involvement Plan, Naval Air Station Meridian and Naval Outlying Landing Field Joe Williams, August 2020
source_notes.note: Official Navy/NAVFAC plan repeats the NAS Meridian timeline and the 1987 renaming of outlying field Bravo as NOLF Joe Williams.

candidates.rationale: The sourced year supports the current exact named feature, not the earlier outlying-field Bravo lineage. A broader pre-1987 operational start should stay unresolved until a source states when Bravo first opened.

source_notes.title: 130th Airlift Wing celebrates 70th Anniversary

source_notes.title: 130th Airlift Wing Fact Sheet
source_notes.note: Official fact sheet identifies the current installation as McLaughlin Air National Guard Base in Charleston, West Virginia.

source_notes.title: AirNav: KCRW - West Virginia International Yeager Airport

candidates.name: Muir Army Airfield

source_notes.title: Fort Indiantown Gap - History
source_notes.note: Official Fort Indiantown Gap history says Muir Army Airfield was constructed during the World War II buildout and the reservation was dedicated March 3, 1941.

source_notes.note: AirNav FAA record identifies the current Muir military-use heliport at Fort Indiantown Gap.

source_notes.note: Official Utah National Guard history says the Utah Air National Guard was founded on Nov. 18, 1946, with federal recognition of the 191st Fighter Squadron at Salt Lake City Municipal Airport.

source_notes.title: Utah Air National Guard base will be renamed for war hero Roland R. Wright
source_notes.note: National Guard article identifies the Utah ANG base on the east side of Salt Lake City International Airport and notes the Nov. 18, 1946 establishment date of the Utah ANG and 191st Fighter Squadron.

source_notes.title: AirNav: KSLC - Salt Lake City International Airport
source_notes.note: AirNav FAA record lists airport activation date 11/1938 and current ANG communications/operations at the same airport.

candidates.rationale: The official Guard history anchors the Air National Guard presence at Salt Lake City Municipal Airport in 1946; the later Roland R. Wright name is a 2014 rename, not the operational start.

candidates.name: Warfield Air National Guard Base

source_notes.title: History of the Maryland Air National Guard - 175th Wing
source_notes.note: Official 175th Wing history says the military facilities at Martin State Airport were formally renamed in honor of Maj. Gen. Edwin Warfield III in 1982, and the base has since been known as Warfield Air National Guard Base.

source_notes.title: AirNav: KMTN - Martin State Airport
source_notes.note: AirNav FAA record lists Martin State Airport activation date 04/1940 and current 175th Wing command-post frequencies.

candidates.rationale: The exact GeoNames name is the post-1982 Warfield ANG Base name, so 1982 is the conservative exact-name start even though military/ANG use of Martin State predates the rename.

source_notes.note: Official Air Combat Command article says a B-2 Spirit crashed Feb. 23, 2008, at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam.

source_notes.note: Official Air Force article summarizes the accident investigation and states the crash occurred on takeoff at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, on Feb. 23, 2008.

candidates.name: Arsenale

source_notes.title: Museo Storico Navale di Venezia - L'arsenale - Marina Militare
source_notes.note: Italian Navy page says the origins of the Arsenale date to 1104, when Doge Falier established a state shipyard.

source_notes.title: Storia dell'Arsenale di Venezia - Comune di Venezia
source_notes.note: Venice municipal history says the Arsenale Vecchio arose in the early 12th century and cautions that the exact 1104 foundation date is conventional.

candidates.rationale: The GeoNames point is the Venice Arsenale naval complex. The candidate records the conventional 1104 origin with medium confidence because municipal history notes that this medieval foundation date is not exact to modern precision.
